description.text:
The promos of Japan's Advanced Generation years: 63 cards, 001/ADV-P to 063/ADV-P, released from January 2003 to February 2004. The Advanced era began with the expansion Expansion Pack and matches the first half of the EX years elsewhere; with it, the T and P suffixes of earlier promos gave way to ADV-P.

They came with CoroCoro Comic and Shogakukan's elementary school magazines, two McDonald's promotions, in early 2003 and early 2004, and twelve Meiji Chocolate cards of Kanto Pokémon in February 2004. The 7-Eleven Pokémon Fair of June 2003 brought 21 cards, most of them two to a Pokémon, with Jirachi as its secret card. Others came from the Pokémon Card Gym start lottery, Battle Road Summer and Autumn 2003, Pokémon Wonderland and the World Hobby Fair 2004.

The others were Sceptile 046, Blaziken 047, Plusle 049 and Minun 050. Each carries the McDonald's logo in its bottom left corner. Hiromichi Sugiyama drew the three Hoenn starters' final forms.

description.text: One of the 12 cards of Meiji's first series of Pokémon card game promos, released in February 2004, one in each box of Meiji chocolate, sealed in a clear cellophane sleeve with a strip of opaque silver paint. Meiji had made its own Pokémon cards for its chocolates since 1997, but these were its first for the card game. All 12 use Ken Sugimori's art and carry Meiji's red logo in the bottom left corner. A second series of 12 followed in June 2004, numbered as PCG-P promos.

description.text: Mitsuhiro Arita's Metang from Pokémon Wonderland, 044/ADV-P, reprinted with a WHF stamp for the 19th Next Generation World Hobby Fair, the Shogakukan group's fair of games and toys. Players got it for taking part in the Pokémon card booth's Point Get Battle or its challenge against the Pokémon Card Laboratory. Its bottom edge calls it a card commemorating taking part in the fair, which was held in Osaka on 18 January, in Tokyo on 24 and 25 January, in Nagoya on 1 February and in Fukuoka on 8 February 2004. It is the last ADV-P promo.
